## p179 A — Equipment transfer east of the Rhine while maintaining radio operation

**Edition context:** Equipment transfer east of the Rhine, with radio service maintained.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-right-rhine-equipment-equipment-transfer-east-of-the-rhine-with-radio-service-maintained"></a>



**Source recovery and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

This order directs equipment identified by the unexpanded label **`U.S.`**
to the nearest replacement unit east of the Rhine. It also requires wireless
station operation to be maintained. `U.S.` is preserved as a source label;
the text does not establish an American origin or a particular equipment type.

The source is Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*,
[printed p179 A, PDF page 182](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view),
with this [visible header and ciphertext](../experiments/november_armistice_orders/sources/p179_A.png):

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
A) KS CZ FG v XF (20.07, November 11th)
RICHI-266
```

</details>

<a id="edition-cases-radio-right-rhine-equipment-conditional-shared-digits"></a>

### Conditional shared digits

The equipment order gains the complete reference **4B49936**, fixing **133/133 labels**. Its existing five-coordinate printed cancellation and seven word substitutions retain their separate costs. The [joint reconstruction](../experiments/nov10_joint_completion/README.md) combines the earlier Marineamt and formation interpretations with the army-number constraint and the mobilization decree; the reversed 7/9 assignment is retained there.

**Conditional interpretation — readable German under the joint square:**

> Dort befind. U S Geraete zur naechsten rechtsrhein. Ers. Abtlg. schaffen. Funkstellenbetrieb muss aufrechterhalten bleiben. Nachrichtenchef 4B49936.

<details>
<summary>Exact conditional labels</summary>

**Edited output — p179_A, conditional shared square; 133/133 fixed positions:**

```text
DORTBEFINDXUXSXGERAETEZURNAECHSTENRECHTSRHEINXERSXABTLGXSCHAFFENXFUNKSTELLENBETRIEBMUSSAUFRECHTERHALTENBLEIBENXNACHRICHTENCHEF4B49936
```

</details>


<a id="edition-cases-radio-right-rhine-equipment-a-cancelled-duplicate-restores-the-printed-frame-length"></a>

### A cancelled duplicate restores the printed frame length

The literal transcription contains **271 coordinates**. Source group 17,
at zero-based positions **80–84**, is visibly struck through. It reads
`ADADG`, exactly duplicating the immediately preceding group. Excluding the
marked copy gives the advertised **266-coordinate frame**.

The cancelled group remains in the literal transcript and in the source
image. Its exclusion counts as **five observed coordinates removed at the
printed cancellation**. It is not reported as a zero-edit source. A close
view of the damaged but readable `X` at source position 190 is also
[preserved](../experiments/november_armistice_orders/sources/p179_A_glyph.png).

Under the unchanged published Nov10–12 square and ranks, the resulting raw
reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — frame excluding the visibly cancelled duplicate group; exclusion priced separately:**

```text
DORTBEFINDXUXSXGERAETEZURNAECHSTENRECHTSRHEINXERSXABTLGXOCHAFKENXFU?OSTELLENB2TRIEBMUSSAUFRECHTERHA?TENBLEIBENXNACHRICHTENC0EF4B4??3?
```

</details>

Seven separately recorded observed-coordinate substitutions give:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — same cancelled-group frame, followed by seven word repairs:**

```text
DORTBEFINDXUXSXGERAETEZURNAECHSTENRECHTSRHEINXERSXABTLGXSCHAFFENXFUNKSTELLENBETRIEBMUSSAUFRECHTERHALTENBLEIBENXNACHRICHTENCHEF4B4??3?
```

</details>

A readable expansion, with abbreviation completions in brackets, is:

**Readable German — after the cancelled-group exclusion and priced word repairs:**

> Dort befind[liche] U.S.-Geräte zur nächsten rechtsrhein[ischen]
> Ers[atz]abtlg. schaffen. Funkstellenbetrieb muss aufrechterhalten
> bleiben. Nachrichtenchef `4B4??3?`.

The three question marks in the closing `4B4??3?` are retained. They arise
from unassigned cells in the published partial square, not missing source
coordinates. The two ordinary-word question marks in the raw reading are
also partial-key outcomes; their editorial repairs change observed
coordinates, rather than filling the key with new letters.

The abbreviation `ABTLG` already includes its final G. The readable display
therefore retains that letter outside editorial brackets and preserves the
entire closing reference, including its fixed labels and three unknowns.

| Literal source slots | Analysis-frame slots | Raw fixed labels | Edition fixed labels | Observed coordinates excluded | Known-coordinate substitutions | Erasure fills |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 271 | 266 | 128 / 133 | 130 / 133 | 5 | 7 | 0 |

There are no added coordinates, block moves or baseline-key changes.
The [inputs](../experiments/november_armistice_orders/inputs.json) and
[certificate](../experiments/november_armistice_orders/certificates.json)
preserve both duplicate groups, the exact exclusion, every substitution,
raw domains and global re-encryption witnesses. Arbitrary completions are
marked as consistency examples, not original numerical readings.

The period key is credited to **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and
Arno Wacker**. The previous unreviewed OCR stream did not yield this coherent
body. The new contribution is the source reading and priced edition;
the bounded publication check is recorded without a universal priority claim.

The other source records on this page are covered in the
[armistice and leave case](#edition-cases-military-armistice-and-leave-orders).

```sh
python experiments/november_armistice_orders/verify.py --verify
```

## Citadel surrender, local armistice terms and home leave

**Sources on this page:** p179 B, p179 C, p179 D1, p179 D2.

<a id="edition-cases-military-armistice-and-leave-orders-citadel-surrender-local-armistice-terms-and-home-leave"></a>



**Source editions: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Four physical parts on Childs p179 concern surrender terms, a request for
the armistice conditions applicable to Mackensen's front, and postponement
of discharge and urgent home leave. The source's dates, abbreviated words,
unresolved reference fields and unusual year form are preserved separately
from the ordinary-word repairs.

The source is Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*,
[printed p179, PDF page 182](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The adjacent A record is a separate
[radio-equipment transfer order](#edition-cases-radio-right-rhine-equipment).

<a id="edition-cases-military-armistice-and-leave-orders-conditional-shared-digits"></a>

### Conditional shared digits

The citadel instruction gains **KM 2583 18G ANCH**, fixing **79/79 labels** after the earlier single word repair. The suffix remains a literal administrative reference. The [joint reconstruction](../experiments/nov10_joint_completion/README.md) combines the earlier Marineamt and formation interpretations with the army-number constraint and the mobilization decree; the reversed 7/9 assignment is retained there.

**Conditional interpretation — readable German under the joint square:**

> Zitadelle: Widerstand aufgeben, Uebergabebedingungen dort festsetzen. K M 2583 18G ANCH.

<details>
<summary>Exact conditional labels</summary>

**Edited output — p179_B, conditional shared square; 79/79 fixed positions:**

```text
ZITADELLEXWIDERSTANDAUFGEBENUEBERGABEBEDINGUNGENDORTFESTSETZENXKMX2583X18GXANCH
```

</details>


<a id="edition-cases-military-armistice-and-leave-orders-b-abandon-resistance-and-determine-surrender-terms"></a>

### B: abandon resistance and determine surrender terms

The [158-coordinate telegram](../experiments/november_armistice_orders/sources/p179_B.png)
has `WAU v LP (15.50, November 11th); KR (15.53)` and a separate `NF NF NF`
postamble outside the ciphertext. Its direct reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
ZITADELLEXWIDERSTANDAUFGEBENUEBERGABEBEDINGUNGENGORTFESTSETZENXKMX2??3X1?GXANCH
```

</details>

One observed-coordinate substitution proposes `DORT` for `GORT`:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
ZITADELLEXWIDERSTANDAUFGEBENUEBERGABEBEDINGUNGENDORTFESTSETZENXKMX2??3X1?GXANCH
```

</details>

The instruction is to abandon resistance at the citadel and set surrender
terms there. The message does not name the citadel's city. Its final
`KMX2??3X1?GXANCH` reference remains unresolved; the three question marks
come from the partial square, with all source coordinates present.

<a id="edition-cases-military-armistice-and-leave-orders-c-what-armistice-conditions-apply-to-this-front"></a>

### C: what armistice conditions apply to this front?

The [232-coordinate source](../experiments/november_armistice_orders/sources/p179_C.png)
has `--- v ZO'N (10.25 p.m., November 11th)` and several routing lines,
including `2000 FUER LP KK 11 KK (11) KR`. The full routing text and the
interstitial `WP WP WP FF NKJ v ZO'N` are preserved in the input record.

The raw output is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
ANOHLXOBERKOMMANDOMACKE1SENUND11XARMEEERBITTENMITTEILUNGDERBESONDERENWAFFENSTILLSTANDSBESINGXFUERHIESIGEFRONTXAOK11X
```

</details>

Three observed-coordinate substitutions repair the two word fragments
`MACKE1SEN→MACKENSEN` and `BESING→BEDING`:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
ANOHLXOBERKOMMANDOMACKENSENUND11XARMEEERBITTENMITTEILUNGDERBESONDERENWAFFENSTILLSTANDSBEDINGXFUERHIESIGEFRONTXAOK11X
```

</details>

Mackensen's high command and the 11th Army ask OHL to communicate the
particular armistice conditions for their front. The abbreviation
`BEDING` is retained, without inserting letters to spell out *Bedingungen*.
B and C use the unchanged published Nov10–12 key.

<a id="edition-cases-military-armistice-and-leave-orders-d-discharge-delayed-and-urgent-home-leave-suspended"></a>

### D: discharge delayed, and urgent home leave suspended

The [two-part source](../experiments/november_armistice_orders/sources/p179_D.png)
is separately headed:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
12th NOVEMBER, 1918.
D) FUER UKS (18.50, November 12th) 2 TLE
```

</details>

Its actual part lengths are **190 and 212 coordinates**, matching their
printed labels. The earlier D1 OCR stream had 191 slots. Manual
retranscription restores the received 190-slot frame, with no insertion
or deletion of the printed source itself.

Both parts read under the unchanged published key labelled **Nov13–15b**.
That label differs from the source's **12 November** heading. The dates
and the successful working-key identity remain recorded together; their
chronology is unresolved.

D1's direct output, with **zero source repairs**, is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
INFLGTRANSPTSCHWIERIGKINHEIMATISTDURCHKMDX????AMANGEORDNENTLASSGLDSTURMJAHRGX1560U61VERSCHOBENX
```

</details>

It reports that transport difficulties at home have caused a previously
ordered discharge of Landsturm year groups to be postponed. The reference
after `KMD` remains unknown. The year-like text **`1560U61`** is preserved
literally. The edition does not normalize it to a historically plausible
year or assign a new digit value.

D2's direct output, also with **zero source repairs**, is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
DRINGENDEHEIMATSURLAUBEHABENBISAUFWEITERESGAENZLICHZUUNTERBLEIBENXCHEFDESGENSTABESNRXRM1A11???GEHOPEZ??0?X
```

</details>

Urgent home leave is to cease entirely until further notice. The signatory
is the chief of the general staff; the remaining reference string is not
completed. The question marks in these two parts are unassigned key cells,
not printed erasures, and their domains share one global square bijection.

The separate [p193 award-class interpretation](../experiments/nov13_joint_completion/README.md)
assigns `VG=2`, giving `RM1A11?2?` in D2. This fixes one further position,
**101/106**, while leaving the reference incomplete and adding no source
repair.

The [inputs](../experiments/november_armistice_orders/inputs.json) and
[certificate](../experiments/november_armistice_orders/certificates.json)
retain full source rows, header differences, all source images and every
digit/`J/Q/Y` occurrence, including changes made only by priced ordinary-word
repairs. Global re-encryption witnesses check compatibility and costs;
their arbitrary missing-key assignments are not proposed original numbers.

The keys are prior work by **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and
Arno Wacker**. B, C and D2 already had unreviewed OCR-derived body candidates,
also represented in the frozen p73 retrieval corpus. D1 gains a coherent
source reading from the corrected transcription length. The bounded
publication check is recorded, with no universal priority claim.

```sh
python experiments/november_armistice_orders/verify.py --verify
```

The optional `--pdf` check regenerates all source crops from the pinned scan
and compares their pixels.
